werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-gish.text:
Gish is the debut by the Smashing Pumpkins, recorded from December 1990 to March 1991 at Smart Studios in Madison, Wisconsin. Butch Vig and Billy Corgan produced it together, on a budget of 20,000 dollars. For Vig, then a little-known producer, having so much time to work on a guitar sound or on harmonies was new. Corgan played almost all the guitar and bass himself. The sessions were a heavy strain on the group.

The music seeks a balance between heavy riffs, as with Black Sabbath and Led Zeppelin, and the sensitivity of British bands such as The Cure. Rhinoceros shows this well: first psychedelic and beautiful, then suddenly heavy with a sharp lead guitar. Corgan called it an album about pain and spiritual growth. The name comes from the silent film star Lillian Gish. The reactions were very positive, and the album later became one of the best-selling independent records of its time.
werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-gish.listen: Listen to Rhinoceros and notice the moment when the soft, dreamy opening turns into heavy guitars and a sharp lead part.

werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-machina-the-m.text:
After the tour for Adore, drummer Jimmy Chamberlin returned to the group. The band members decided that there would be one more album and one more tour before they stopped for good. Billy Corgan devised a concept album about a rock star, Zero, who hears the voice of God and calls himself Glass. The group recorded in Chicago, with Flood as co-producer. When bassist D'Arcy Wretzky left, Corgan and James Iha took over the bass.

Machina/The Machines of God was released on 29 February 2000 on Virgin. The album built on the electronic side of Adore, but also let hard guitars be heard again. The concept remained largely unfinished, and the lyrics are mostly about the end of the group and about survival. The reception was generally favourable. The sequel, Machina II, was released by the group themselves and given away to fans over the internet.
werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-machina-the-m.listen: Listen to With Every Light and notice the faint acoustic guitar and the lyric in which Corgan sings that it is almost over.

werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-mellon-collie.text:
After the long tour for Siamese Dream, Billy Corgan started writing straight away. The band wanted to make a double album, partly inspired by the Beatles' White Album, and approached it as if it might be their last. Producer Butch Vig was replaced by Flood and Alan Moulder. In April 1995 the group started in a rehearsal room, where much of the rhythm work was recorded. Guitarist James Iha and bassist D'arcy Wretzky played a bigger role than before. So many songs came about that dozens of finished pieces had to be left off the album.

The album was released on 23 October 1995 on Virgin Records, with 28 tracks on two CDs. It blends art rock, grunge, alternative rock and heavy metal. It entered at number one on the American chart. Singles included Bullet with Butterfly Wings, 1979 and Tonight, Tonight. Critics praised the ambition and the album is regarded as one of the best of the 1990s.
werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-mellon-collie.listen: Listen to Bullet with Butterfly Wings, the first single, and notice how broad the album's style already sounds here. Then compare it with another song from the record.

werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-oceania.text:
Oceania was released on 19 June 2012 via Martha's Music. The record belongs to Teargarden by Kaleidyscope, the large project in which the group put out individual songs for free on the internet for years. Billy Corgan now wanted to make an album, as an album within the album, because releasing one song at a time had, in his view, run its course. He produced it together with Bjorn Thorsrud. It was the first record with guitarist Jeff Schroeder and the only one with bassist Nicole Fiorentino and drummer Mike Byrne.

The lyrics deal with alienation in love and in modern culture. The songs The Celestials and Panopticon were released as singles. Schroeder wanted it to sound somewhat more spacious and dreamy than earlier records. Most critics reacted positively and called it Corgan's best record in a long time. The album entered at number four on the Billboard 200.
werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-oceania.listen: Listen to The Celestials, the first single, and see whether you can hear if the song sounds spacious and dreamy, as guitarist Jeff Schroeder wanted.

werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-siamese-dream.text: On 27 July 1993 Siamese Dream was released by The Smashing Pumpkins from Chicago. Singer and guitarist Billy Corgan piled dozens of guitar parts on top of one another into a wall of sound. The songs alternate between lovely and furious. The album became a great success and made the band one of the most important of 1990s alternative rock.
werk/the-smashing-pumpkins-siamese-dream.listen: In Today a cheerful guitar motif sounds, but the lyrics are about the best day of your life, while you actually want to die. Music and lyrics pull apart.

werk/the-smiths-meat-is-murder.text:
Meat Is Murder is the second studio album by The Smiths and was released on 11 February 1985 on Rough Trade. Recording ran from mid-1984 to December in London and at Ridge Farm Studio in Surrey. Guitarist Johnny Marr made the demos at home in his flat in Earl's Court. Singer Morrissey gave him and engineer Stephen Street his own records of BBC sound effects to take samples from. The band went into the album with confidence, after the success of the debut and the compilation Hatful of Hollow.

The sound is more varied than before, with influences of indie rock and post-punk. The lyrics are more political and deal with vegetarianism, corporal punishment and loneliness. The cover shows an American soldier from the Vietnam War, with a helmet bearing the words Meat Is Murder. It became the group's only studio album to reach number one in Great Britain. The reactions were mostly positive, although some critics found the album too monotonous.
werk/the-smiths-meat-is-murder.listen: Listen to the title song Meat Is Murder and notice how the lyrics state the position on meat and animals directly.

werk/the-smiths-strangeways-here-we-come.text:
Strangeways, Here We Come is the fourth and final studio album by The Smiths. It was released on 28 September 1987, a few months after the group had split up. Recording took place in March at Wool Hall in Bath, under producer Stephen Street, to complete the contract with Rough Trade. Guitarist Johnny Marr wanted to move away from the jingle-jangle sound with which the band was associated. He used fewer overdubs and sought new influences, including the Beatles and the Walker Brothers.

The sound is more varied, with synthesised saxophone, strings on keyboards and drum machine. On Death of a Disco Dancer, Morrissey plays piano, the only time on an album by the group. On Stop Me If You Think You've Heard This One Before, Marr dropped a knife onto his guitar for a slapping effect. The record reached number two in Great Britain and is regarded by all four members as their best work.
werk/the-smiths-strangeways-here-we-come.listen: Listen to Death of a Disco Dancer and notice Morrissey's piano, which you hear on no other album by the group.

werk/the-smiths-the-queen-is-dead.text:
The Queen Is Dead is the third album by The Smiths. After Meat Is Murder, the band withdrew to Greater Manchester to escape the pressure of London and of their record label Rough Trade. Johnny Marr and Morrissey wrote much of it at Marr's house in Bowdon. Recording ran from July to December 1985, including at RAK Studios in London and Jacobs Studios in Farnham. Morrissey and Marr produced it themselves, with Stephen Street as engineer. The title comes from the novel Last Exit to Brooklyn by Hubert Selby Jr.

The music blends indie rock and post-punk. In the title song, Mike Joyce and Street made a loop of tom-toms with a sampler, while Marr played feedback through a wah-wah pedal. The album was released in June 1986 and reached number 2 in England. Critics praised Marr's guitar work and Morrissey's witty, emotional lyrics. In 2013 NME declared it the best album of all time.
werk/the-smiths-the-queen-is-dead.listen: In The Boy with the Thorn In His Side, listen to Johnny Marr's guitar playing: notice how the melody keeps singing throughout the whole song.

werk/the-smiths-the-smiths.text:
In 1982 Johnny Marr asked Morrissey to start a band together. They wrote the first songs in Marr's attic room. After signing to Rough Trade, the band recorded a first version in 1983 with producer Troy Tate in a hot basement in London. Those recordings were rejected. John Porter recorded everything again, in September 1983, between gigs. The record cost about 6,000 pounds and was released on 20 February 1984.

Marr's clear, jangling guitar stands alongside Morrissey's literary and melancholy lyrics about unrequited love, loneliness and social discontent. Reel Around the Fountain and Suffer Little Children caused a stir because of their lyrics. Many songs omit the traditional chorus and opt for long narrative verses. Critical reception in 1984 was mixed: praise for the compositions, criticism of the production. Later the debut was seen as a milestone and as one of the most influential British records of the 1980s. It reached number two in England.
werk/the-smiths-the-smiths.listen: Listen to Reel Around the Fountain and notice Morrissey's low, restrained singing, which gives the song of nearly six minutes its wistful tone.

werk/the-specials-guilty-til-proved-inno.text:
Guilty 'til Proved Innocent! from 1998 is the first studio album of new songs by The Specials since 1984, written by both original and new members. Neville Staple, Roddy Byers, Lynval Golding and Horace Panter were joined by Mark Adams, Adam Birch and Jon Read. Drummer Charley Bembridge of The Selecter played on it, having performed live with the group since 1994. Stoker produced the record.

Inevitably the album was compared with the 1979 to 1981 line-up, but the reviews were much more favourable than for the covers album Today's Specials, and it was often called a return to form. It's You was the single for Modern Rock radio. Running Away is based on Monkey Man by Toots & the Maytals, which the band covered on the 1979 debut album.
werk/the-specials-guilty-til-proved-inno.listen: Listen to Fearful and notice the extra voices of Tim Armstrong and Lars Frederiksen.

werk/the-specials-in-the-studio.text:
In the Studio was the third album by the British ska revival group, but it was released in June 1984 under the name The Special AKA. It took more than two years to make and by the time it came out, the original line-up had long since broken up. Jerry Dammers produced the album. Besides the regular members, many guests took part, including trombonist Rico Rodriguez. Elvis Costello produced Nelson Mandela.

The sound is gloomier than on the first two records, with a dark view of the world and political lyrics. Nelson Mandela became an international hit, although the album sold less than its predecessors and reached the British top 35. NME ranked it number three in its list of the best albums of 1984. A reviewer in Sounds spoke of Dammers's most powerful statement to date. Later critics see it not as a noble failure, but as the fitting conclusion to the group's career.
werk/the-specials-in-the-studio.listen: Listen to Nelson Mandela and notice how cheerful the music sounds, while the song is about the imprisonment of a political leader.

werk/the-specials-more-specials.text:
After the success of the debut, Jerry Dammers took charge of the Specials and wanted to move away from ska. He became fascinated by muzak and lounge music, which he had heard in hotel bars and lifts while touring America. Recording in the summer of 1980 took place in Coventry, with Dammers himself as producer. The album was built up mainly in the studio, one instrument at a time. This caused tension: the members had different tastes, from northern soul to rockabilly, and the band largely fell apart in 1981.

The result is eclectic. Side one contains ska, northern soul and reggae, and the album opens and closes with Enjoy Yourself (It's Later Than You Think). Side two has the muzak atmosphere. The lyrics are often bleak and political, but with humour. The album reached number five in England and was later cited as an influence on trip hop.
werk/the-specials-more-specials.listen: Listen to Enjoy Yourself (It's Later Than You Think) and notice the cheerful drums and horns. Try to hear how the carefree title hides something dark.

werk/the-specials-specials.text:
The debut album by The Specials was released on 19 October 1979 on Jerry Dammers's 2 Tone label. Elvis Costello produced it. The record captures the anger and boredom of young people in the grim inner cities of 1970s Britain. It contains original songs and covers of old Jamaican ska. The band reworked the sound of the 1960s: less percussion and smaller horn sections, with punk anger and the guitar at the front of the mix.

The opening track A Message to You Rudy had been a single by Dandy Livingstone in 1967. Trombonist Rico Rodriguez, who had already played on old Jamaican recordings, was on hand this time too. Too Much Too Young appeared in a live version on an EP that reached number one. The British press reacted in a mixed way, but NME placed the record in its top ten of 1979. Later it was seen as the definitive moment of British ska.
werk/the-specials-specials.listen: Listen to A Message to You Rudy and notice the trombone of Rico Rodriguez. He also played on the original recording.

werk/the-specials-today-s-specials.text:
Today's Specials is a covers album from 1996 and the first studio album by the Specials since 1984, although not the whole original line-up took part. Neville Staple, Roddy Byers, Lynval Golding and Horace Panter were joined by Mark Adams, Adam Birch and session musicians. The lead vocals are mainly by Staple and Golding, and Staple's daughter Sheena sings backing vocals.

Pressure Drop and Hypocrite were released as singles in the United Kingdom. The record did not receive good reviews from the media and fans: many reviewers were put off by the abundant use of synthesizers and programmed drums. Staple himself says that some recordings were actually produced demos and regrets that they ended up on the album.
werk/the-specials-today-s-specials.listen: Listen to Pressure Drop, one of the two singles, and notice the synthesizers and programmed drums that critics objected to.

werk/the-stone-roses-the-stone-roses.text:
The debut by the Manchester band was recorded mainly between June 1988 and February 1989 at Battery Studios in London, with producer John Leckie, who had been suggested by bassist Mani. Leckie found the demos too fast and the vocals too echoey, and had the group rearrange songs with intros, outros and slower tempos. On I Am the Resurrection he advised against ending with a loud feedback jam as they did live; the song was given a melodic ending.

The record did not catch on immediately, but grew along with the group's gigs and became a key work of the Madchester and baggy scene. The music sounds like guitar pop with melodies in the manner of the Beatles and chiming guitars reminiscent of the Byrds. Elizabeth My Dear borrows its melody from the old song Scarborough Fair. Later critics saw the album as one of the best of all time, and according to a 2006 book more than four million copies have been sold worldwide.
werk/the-stone-roses-the-stone-roses.listen: Listen to I Am the Resurrection and notice the ending: live the band finished with loud feedback, but on the album they chose a melodic close.

werk/the-stooges-fun-house.text:
The Stooges' debut had received mixed reviews in 1969 and sold little. Label boss Jac Holzman saw more in the MC5, but nevertheless asked Don Gallucci, former keyboard player of the Kingsmen, to produce the second album. Gallucci doubted whether the band could be captured on tape. Recording took place in May 1970 at Elektra Sound Recorders in Los Angeles. After a failed first day, band and producer stripped the studio of partitions and ordinary equipment, so that they could play as they did on stage. One song was recorded per day, with at most four takes.

The sound is raw: because there is no screening, the snare drum rattles along with the bass amplifier. Iggy Pop named Howlin' Wolf as a major inspiration. On the second side come loose song structures and the saxophone of Steve Mackay. The album at first sold poorly, but has since acquired great cult status and is regarded as important for the development of punk.
werk/the-stooges-fun-house.listen: Listen to the closing track L.A. Blues. Notice how it runs out into a torrent of noise and confused, doubled drums.

werk/the-stranglers-black-and-white.text:
Black and White was released in May 1978 and was the band's third album. Like the two previous records it was produced by Martin Rushent. The group now opted for a more experimental approach to song structure and time signatures: Curfew is written in 7/4. Sweden even got a Swedish-language version, Sverige, for the Swedish market. Death and Night and Blood takes its title from a sentence in a novel by Yukio Mishima.

The first 75,000 LPs came with a free white single containing, among other things, Walk On By, an adaptation of the song by Burt Bacharach and Hal David. The press was positive; NME called the A-side the best work the band had ever made. Later critics judged it in different ways. Some thought it the weakest of the first three records, others saw an album that had already moved beyond punk and that left traces in Gang of Four and Joy Division.
werk/the-stranglers-black-and-white.listen: Listen to Curfew and try to feel the time signature: the song is in 7/4, so the count runs slightly differently from what you are used to.

werk/the-stranglers-rattus-norvegicus.text:
This debut album by The Stranglers was released in April 1977 and was recorded in one week by producer Martin Rushent. The record gives a picture of the group's live set at the time. The original title was Dead on Arrival, but it was replaced at the last moment by the Latin name for the brown rat. The inscription The Stranglers IV was intended to sow confusion.

The songs are about rows with a girlfriend, pub crowds in London and life in a squat. Peaches is the inner monologue of a man watching girls on the beach. Down in the Sewer is a long closer in four parts, in which the sewers represent London. The record was one of the best-selling albums of the punk era in Great Britain. NME placed it tenth among the best albums of the year in 1977, and later lists mention it too.
werk/the-stranglers-rattus-norvegicus.listen: Listen to Down in the Sewer and notice the four parts of which the song is built, from Falling to Rat's Rally.

werk/the-stranglers-the-raven.text:
The Raven is the fourth studio album by The Stranglers and was released on 21 September 1979 on United Artists. For the first time it was not produced by Martin Rushent, but by the band themselves with engineer Alan Winstanley. The first two tracks, much of the sleeve illustration and the title refer to Norse mythology.

The lyrics deal with a variety of subjects: Japanese ritual suicide in Ice, heroin use in Don't Bring Harry, the Iranian revolution in Shah Shah a Go Go and genetic manipulation in Genetix. In Dead Loss Angeles, Hugh Cornwell plays bass alongside Jean-Jacques Burnel, without guitar. Duchess was the first and most successful single. The album was first released with a limited 3D sleeve.
werk/the-stranglers-the-raven.listen: Listen to Dead Loss Angeles and notice the heavy bass line, because there is no guitar on this track. Hear how two basses carry the song.

werk/the-strokes-is-this-it.text:
In 2001 the New York band had already put themselves on the map with the EP The Modern Age. After a bidding war they signed to RCA and began with producer Gil Norton, but the results sounded too clean and too pretentious and were thrown away. Gordon Raphael then recorded the debut in his basement studio Transporterraum in Manhattan, in six weeks in March and April. Singer Julian Casablancas wanted a sound like that of a band from the past who had travelled to the future in a time machine.

Most of the songs were recorded in a single take, with raw guitars and a tight rhythm. The lyrics describe the lives and relationships of young city dwellers. After the attacks of 11 September, New York City Cops was removed from the CD in the United States. Is This It received broad praise for its two-guitar interplay and is regarded as a turning point for guitar music in the new millennium.
werk/the-strokes-is-this-it.listen: Listen to Last Nite and notice how the two guitars and the tight rhythm together make a raw, danceable sound.

werk/the-supremes-a-bit-of-liverpool.text:
A Bit of Liverpool is the third studio album by the Supremes, released in the autumn of 1964 on Motown, in the United Kingdom under the title With Love (From Us to You). Berry Gordy produced it, and Hal Davis and Marc Gordon handled the mix. The album contains covers of recent hits by British Invasion groups, plus two songs by Motown artists that had been covered by British groups: Do You Love Me and You've Really Got a Hold on Me.

The album just missed the American top twenty, at number 21. The critical response was poor. A reviewer for the San Francisco Examiner wrote that only You Can't Do That deserved first place and that the rest were just there. In 2008 the author Mark Ribowsky called it a jolly old mess, and The Encyclopedia of Popular Music gave it two out of five stars.
werk/the-supremes-a-bit-of-liverpool.listen: Listen to A Hard Days Night and notice how the three singers sing a Beatles song, and compare it with the original.

werk/the-supremes-we-remember-sam-cooke.text:
In April 1965 Motown released this album as a tribute to Sam Cooke, who had died in December of the previous year. It is the fifth studio album by The Supremes and consists entirely of songs by Cooke. Harvey Fuqua, Hal Davis and Marc Gordon produced it.

Diana Ross sings the lead parts, except on (Ain't That) Good News, where Florence Ballard takes the lead and Ross sings backing vocals. The group tackle well-known songs such as You Send Me, Chain Gang, Bring It On Home to Me and A Change Is Gonna Come. The album belongs to a series of themed albums that Motown made in those years. It was the second most successful of that series and reached fifth place on the Billboard R&B chart.
werk/the-supremes-we-remember-sam-cooke.listen: Listen to (Ain't That) Good News and notice that here it is not Diana Ross but Florence Ballard who sings the lead part.

werk/the-supremes-where-did-our-love-go.text:
Where Did Our Love Go is the second album by The Supremes, released in 1964 on Motown. It collects singles and B-sides from 1963 and 1964. Most of the songs were written and produced by Holland, Dozier and Holland. Smokey Robinson, Norman Whitfield and Robert Gordy each produced one or more tracks.

The album contains three songs that became the group's first American number ones: Where Did Our Love Go, Baby Love and Come See About Me. It also features When the Lovelight Starts Shining Through His Eyes, their first top 40 hit. The vocals are by Diana Ross, Florence Ballard and Mary Wilson. The records featured Motown's session musicians, the Funk Brothers, including bassist James Jamerson and pianist Earl Van Dyke. In Where Did Our Love Go, vibraphone and foot stomping can also be heard.
werk/the-supremes-where-did-our-love-go.listen: Listen to Where Did Our Love Go and notice the rhythm beneath the vocals. Can you hear the foot stomping and the vibraphone alongside the bass?

werk/the-temptations-cloud-nine.text:
Cloud Nine from 1969 was a turning point for The Temptations. It was the first complete studio album with Dennis Edwards, who had replaced David Ruffin after he was fired in June 1968. Producer Norman Whitfield took the group into psychedelic soul. The idea came from Otis Williams, who had talked about the funky style of Sly and the Family Stone and felt that the group's sound needed to be renewed. Until then they had had success with ballads such as My Girl.

In the title track all five members take turns as lead singer, over a funk-like accompaniment with wah-wah guitar. Run Away Child, Running Wild grows into a nine-minute epic, with an instrumental jam in the second half. The change of style divided older fans, but the album reached number four on the American pop chart and earned the group their first Grammy in 1969.
werk/the-temptations-cloud-nine.listen: Listen to Cloud Nine and notice how the singers pass the lead part to one another. Also hear the wah-wah guitar beneath the vocals.

werk/the-temptations-meet-the-temptation.text:
Meet the Temptations from 1964 was the group's first album on Gordy, Motown's label. It is not a session but a collection of singles and B-sides, including The Way You Do the Things You Do, the first hit. Only on that track does David Ruffin sing, who had been with the group for just three months. On the other tracks you hear Al Bryant, who had been fired in December 1963.

Most of the songs come from the slow early period, in which Motown staff spoke of the hitless Temptations. Paul Williams sings most of the lead parts, and Eddie Kendricks has a few. Melvin Franklin and Otis Williams also get room for lead lines, ad libs and harmony singing. The record was first released only in mono; a stereo mix followed in 1966.
werk/the-temptations-meet-the-temptation.listen: Listen to Aiming At Your Heart and notice how the lead singer is surrounded by the harmony singing of the rest of the group.

werk/the-temptations-temptin-temptations.text:
The Temptin' Temptations from 1965 is the group's third studio album on Gordy, Motown's label. Seven of the twelve tracks had previously been released as a single or B-side. On the singles from 1964, Eddie Kendricks sings the lead. I'll Be in Trouble was written and produced by Smokey Robinson; Girl (Why You Wanna Make Me Blue) is a production by Norman Whitfield.

In Since I Lost My Baby, a wistful ballad by Robinson and Pete Moore, David Ruffin sings about a world in which everything is fine except love. Don't Look Back, led by Paul Williams, was actually the original A-side of a single, became a hit on the R&B charts and closed the live shows for years. The song is now better known than My Baby.
werk/the-temptations-temptin-temptations.listen: Listen to Since I Lost My Baby and notice how Ruffin's voice carries the wistfulness of the lyrics.

werk/the-temptations-the-temptations-sin.text:
This is the Temptations' second album for Motown, released in 1965 on the Gordy label. All the songs were written and produced by Smokey Robinson, sometimes together with other members of the Miracles. Some are covers of songs that Robinson had previously made for the Miracles or for Mary Wells. The rest were first recorded by the group themselves.

The record contains three hit singles. The Way You Do the Things You Do has Eddie Kendricks as lead singer. In It's Growing and the group's best-known song, My Girl, David Ruffin sings, who was new to the group. The Funk Brothers provide the instrumentation and the Detroit Symphony Orchestra plays the strings.
werk/the-temptations-the-temptations-sin.listen: Listen to Aiming at Your Heart and notice how the group's vocals and the band's accompaniment together carry a Motown song by Smokey Robinson.

werk/the-velvet-underground-loaded.text:
Atlantic asked the Velvet Underground for an album full of hits, and the title refers to that, with a second meaning that you can also be high. The songs were therefore deliberately intended to be short and radio-friendly. Lou Reed left the group in August 1970, before the album came out, and continued to maintain that it had been edited without his permission. A section of Sweet Jane, for instance, was cut. Drummer Maureen Tucker did not play because she was pregnant. The drums came mainly from Doug Yule, the engineer Adrian Barber and two session musicians. Yule sang four songs himself, including Who Loves the Sun.

The record was the group's fourth album and the last with any of the original members. Neither the album nor the singles reached the charts. Only afterwards did it receive much praise, and for many fans it counts as the band's last real record. Rolling Stone ranked it number 110 among the best albums in 2012.
werk/the-velvet-underground-loaded.listen: Listen to Sweet Jane and notice how compact and direct the song is: it was built to be a hit.

werk/the-velvet-underground-squeeze.text:
Squeeze is the fifth and final studio album by the Velvet Underground, recorded in the autumn of 1972 and released by Polydor in February 1973. None of the original band remained. Doug Yule, who had replaced John Cale in 1968, wrote all eleven songs and recorded the album almost entirely himself. Drummer Maureen Tucker was to take part, but was sent away by manager Steve Sesnick.

The album did not reach the charts and quickly disappeared. The British music paper NME spoke of a Velvets album in name only. After a short tour of England, Yule put an end to the group. Only later came a mild reappraisal: in 2011 one writer called it a remarkable listening experience if you forget the troublesome background. The British band Squeeze took its name from it.
werk/the-velvet-underground-squeeze.listen: Listen to Friends, a song later covered by the band Luna. Ask yourself what you hear that fits the Velvet Underground of old, and what does not.

werk/the-velvet-underground-white-light-.text:
White Light/White Heat is the second album by the Velvet Underground and was released on 30 January 1968 on Verve Records. It was the last album with John Cale. Lou Reed had fired Andy Warhol, Steve Sesnick became manager and Tom Wilson produced. In September 1967 it was recorded in a short time at Mayfair Sound Studios in Manhattan, following the example of the loud live performance. With new Vox amplifiers and distortion pedals, all the meters were in the red, and the result sounded distorted and compressed. Most of the band members were unhappy with it.

The lyrics deal with sex, amphetamine and transvestites. The album ends with Sister Ray, a largely improvised song of seventeen minutes. It sold less than the debut and many critics rejected it, but the emphasis on distortion later became an example for punk, shoegaze and noise rock. In 2020 it ranked number 272 in Rolling Stone's list.
werk/the-velvet-underground-white-light-.listen: Listen to Sister Ray and notice the absence of a bass guitar. Can you hear Cale's organ and the guitars raging through one another, while the drums almost drop away?

werk/the-weeknd-beauty-behind-the-madnes.text:
Beauty Behind the Madness, the second studio album by the Canadian singer The Weeknd, was released in August 2015. His first album Kiss Land had been well received, but he considered it a commercial disappointment. A collaboration with Ariana Grande and producer Max Martin, Love Me Harder, became his first top ten hit. That showed him that he could make pop music in his own way. With Martin and others he wrote, among other songs, In the Night and Can't Feel My Face.

The record shifts from dark alternative R&B to a sound that is more pop, with influences of disco, funk and soul. Critics heard the influence of Michael Jackson in it. Guests are Labrinth, Ed Sheeran and Lana Del Rey. The Hills and Can't Feel My Face reached first place on the Billboard Hot 100. The album was his first number one in the United States and won a Grammy for Best Urban Contemporary Album.
werk/the-weeknd-beauty-behind-the-madnes.listen: Listen to Can't Feel My Face and notice the danceable, disco-tinged bass line, which almost recalls Michael Jackson, while the lyrics are darker than the music suggests.

werk/the-weeknd-blinding-lights.text: On 29 November 2019 Blinding Lights by The Weeknd was released. The credits list five writers, including Max Martin and Oscar Holter. The song sounds like a record from 1985: a synthesizer riff as an intro and a drum machine with the sound of the eighties, the Stock Aitken Waterman formula in a new guise. In 2021 Billboard declared it the most successful song in the history of the Hot 100.
werk/the-weeknd-blinding-lights.listen: The song opens straight away with a synthesizer riff that is already a hook in itself. Compare it with Never Gonna Give You Up.

werk/the-weeknd-dawn-fm.text:
After After Hours from 2020, The Weeknd began a new album straight away. An earlier plan, inspired by his gloomy mood during the pandemic, he threw away because it was emotionally too heavy. Dawn FM was released on 7 January 2022. He produced it himself, together with, among others, Max Martin, Oneohtrix Point Never, Oscar Holter, Swedish House Mafia and Calvin Harris.

The album is a radio station for people stuck in purgatory, as he explained it himself. Jim Carrey speaks as the presenter between the songs. The music is predominantly cheerful: dance-pop and synth-pop with influences of new wave, funk and 1980s electronic dance music. Take My Breath was the first single. Tyler, the Creator and Lil Wayne take part as guests. Reviewers praised the production, the structure and the melodies.
werk/the-weeknd-dawn-fm.listen: In Take My Breath, listen to the synthesizers. Notice how strongly they recall the pop music of the 1980s.

werk/the-weeknd-hurry-up-tomorrow.text:
Hurry Up Tomorrow is the sixth studio album by the Canadian singer the Weeknd and was released on 31 January 2025 on XO and Republic Records. It goes with the film of the same name and completes the trilogy that began with After Hours (2020) and Dawn FM (2022). In September 2022 he lost his voice during a performance at SoFi Stadium, after which album and film were thoroughly revised, according to him. He hinted that this may be his last album under his stage name.

The music is mainly synth-pop and R&B, with excursions into, among other things, Brazilian funk and hip hop. Guests include Anitta, Justice, Travis Scott, Florence and the Machine, Future, Playboi Carti, Giorgio Moroder and Lana Del Rey. The singles were Timeless, São Paulo and Cry for Me. The album debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and topped the charts in sixteen countries. Critics praised the production, the lyrics and the vocals.
werk/the-weeknd-hurry-up-tomorrow.listen: Listen to Timeless, one of the singles, and notice the production and the singing for which critics had praise.

werk/the-weeknd-kiss-land.text:
Kiss Land was the first studio album by the Canadian singer The Weeknd and was released in September 2013 on XO and Republic Records. Before that he had made a name for himself with three mixtapes. The album is about life on tour, a world that he built in his head. He drew inspiration from filmmakers such as John Carpenter, David Cronenberg and Ridley Scott, who know how to put fear on screen. The album was meant to feel like a horror film. The production was handled mainly by DannyBoyStyles, the singer himself and DaHeala.

The music revolves around his soft falsetto voice, dark synthesizers, guitars in an 80s vein and menacing drum patterns. Live For is the only track with a guest, Drake. The reviews were mostly positive, although some critics felt it resembled the mixtapes too much. The album entered at number two on the Billboard 200. Entertainment Weekly ranked it fifth in its list of the best albums of 2013.
werk/the-weeknd-kiss-land.listen: Listen to Kiss Land and notice the menacing atmosphere of the synthesizers and the drums, which support the singer's horror story.

werk/the-white-stripes-elephant.text:
In April and May 2002 The White Stripes recorded this album at Toe Rag Studios in London, a cold and uncomfortable studio in Hackney. Jack White produced it himself, on an 8-track recorder and with vintage equipment; no computers were involved. Recording took about two weeks. Because the previous album White Blood Cells had become unexpectedly popular, the release was pushed back from the autumn of 2002 to the spring of 2003.

The songs are about the death of the sweetheart in American pop culture. Seven Nation Army, The Hardest Button to Button and I Just Don't Know What to Do with Myself became singles, and the first gave sales a considerable boost. Seven Nation Army was recorded live, with Jack's guitar through two amplifiers on separate tracks. The critical response was glowing, the album won a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album and is regarded as a key work of the garage rock revival of the 2000s.
werk/the-white-stripes-elephant.listen: Listen to Seven Nation Army and notice how big the song sounds when you hear only one guitar, one drum kit and one voice.

werk/the-white-stripes-white-blood-cells.text:
In February 2001 the duo recorded for three days at Easley McCain Recording in Memphis, in shifts of twelve to thirteen hours. Jack White produced it himself; the recording cost 5,000 dollars and was deliberately fast, to capture the raw tension of playing live. It was the first time the band worked in a 24-track studio, and Jack asked the engineer more than once not to make it sound too pretty. Before that the pair had made two albums in the Detroit music scene.

The lyrics deal with love, hope, betrayal and paranoia. Hotel Yorba, Fell In Love with a Girl and Dead Leaves and the Dirty Ground were released as singles. The title and the cover refer to disillusionment with fame and the commercial music industry. Critics were glowing, and the album brought Jack and Meg White to the forefront of the indie and garage rock of the 2000s.
werk/the-white-stripes-white-blood-cells.listen: Listen to Fell In Love with a Girl and notice how bare and raw it sounds: it is all about guitar, drums and voice, without frills.

werk/the-who-a-quick-one.text:
A Quick One is the second album by The Who and was released on 9 December 1966. It departs from the emphasis on R&B on the debut My Generation. A deal with a publisher gave each band member an advance of 500 pounds for writing two songs. As a result not only Pete Townshend but also John Entwistle, Keith Moon and Roger Daltrey contributed to the writing, and this is the album on which Townshend dominates least. Kit Lambert produced it in London in the autumn of 1966.

The opening track Run Run Run is a stomping hard rocker with a guitar solo full of feedback. Boris the Spider by Entwistle became his best-known song. Cobwebs and Strange was played by the band members on wind instruments. The album closes with A Quick One, While He's Away, a nine-minute suite in six parts about infidelity and forgiveness. It formed the first step towards the later rock operas Tommy and Quadrophenia.
werk/the-who-a-quick-one.listen: Listen to A Quick One, While He's Away and notice how the story is told in six parts. Can you hear where one part turns into the next?

werk/the-who-face-dances.text:
Three years after the death of Keith Moon, the band released an album in 1981 with new drummer Kenney Jones. In the United States it came out on Warner Bros., a new company, and in Great Britain on Polydor. The producer was Bill Szymczyk. The title replaced The Who at the last moment: Pete Townshend jokingly called moving a match between a friend's teeth face dances. The Face Dancers from Dune may also have been on his mind.

The cover consists of sixteen small paintings of the four band members, made by sixteen British artists commissioned by Peter Blake, including David Hockney and Richard Hamilton. You Better You Bet was the first single and its video was one of the first that MTV played in 1981. The reviews were mixed, including in Rolling Stone, but the album reached number two on the British chart.
werk/the-who-face-dances.listen: Listen to You Better You Bet, the first single, and notice the drumming of Kenney Jones, the new drummer after Moon's death.

werk/the-who-my-generation.text:
My Generation is the debut album by the Who, released on 3 December 1965 by Brunswick. The record was made right after the singles I Can't Explain and My Generation. In the spring of 1965 recording began in the days of Maximum R&B, with covers of James Brown such as I Don't Mind and Please Please Please. Later the group opted for new songs by guitarist Pete Townshend, which were recorded in October.

The group themselves later considered the record a rush job that did not capture their live shows well. Even so, critics now call it one of the best rock albums, above all because of its hard sound, which was unusual for the time and heralded punk and heavy metal. My Generation itself is raw and aggressive, while The Kids Are Alright is a more refined pop song with chiming guitars and three-part singing. The album reached number 5 in Great Britain.
werk/the-who-my-generation.listen: Listen to My Generation and notice how raw and aggressive the band sounds, and compare that with the chiming guitars and multi-part singing of The Kids Are Alright.

werk/the-who-quadrophenia.text:
For the Who, 1972 was the quietest year since their formation. After Tommy and Who's Next, Pete Townshend was looking for a new story, and he found it in the mods of 1965. He devised Jimmy, a young mod from London, composed of six early fans and with a fourfold split personality, to which the title alludes. The new studio was not finished, so the band used Ronnie Lane's mobile studio. During the work the relationship with manager Kit Lambert finally broke down.

The double album was written entirely by Townshend and leans on his synthesizers, sound effects and Entwistle's layered horns. Is It in My Head and Love Reign O'er Me date from as early as May 1972. The story ends with Jimmy sitting on a rock in the sea in the rain, with an open ending. The record was received positively and later gave a push to the mod revival, with a successful film in 1979.
werk/the-who-quadrophenia.listen: Listen to Love, Reign O'er Me, the close of the record, and notice how Jimmy's story ends here: with a rock, the rain and an ending that stays open.

werk/the-who-the-who-by-numbers.text:
The Who by Numbers was released on 3 October 1975, the band's first album on Polydor. Pete Townshend was suffering from writer's block. He had just turned thirty, wondered whether he was too old for rock 'n' roll and felt alienated from the music business. The songs are therefore more personal and more inward-looking than earlier work, and sometimes very dark. After the tour for Quadrophenia the band had not played live for more than a year.

Producer Glyn Johns, who had also made Who's Next, had to work hard because the band members had little appetite and the recording was often interrupted. Squeeze Box became a hit and was the only song to remain a fixture on stage. John Entwistle drew the cover, on which the band members appear as join-the-dots drawings. The Village Voice placed the album tenth in the critics' year-end poll. Roger Daltrey later called it his favourite.
werk/the-who-the-who-by-numbers.listen: Listen to Squeeze Box and notice how light and playful it sounds, while the rest of the album is so sombre.

werk/the-who-the-who-sell-out.text:
The Who Sell Out was released on 15 December 1967. In the summer of that year the managers Kit Lambert and Chris Stamp devised a concept album modelled on a pirate radio station. The mods, the group's early audience, had grown up with such stations, which were banned by law in August 1967. The album therefore pretends to be a broadcast by Radio London, with jingles and fake adverts between the songs. Lambert produced it. The title is meant ironically, because at that time the group really did make advertisements.

Most of the songs were written by Pete Townshend, three come from John Entwistle and one from Speedy Keen. I Can See for Miles was the only single and became the band's biggest hit. The album closes with Rael, a short mini-opera in several parts. According to the source, lawsuits over the real brand names followed. Critics praised the album widely, and some see it as the group's best.
werk/the-who-the-who-sell-out.listen: Listen to Heinz Baked Beans, the second track. It is a fake advert for beans recorded as a real song: notice how seriously it is delivered.

werk/the-who-tommy.text:
Pete Townshend had been looking since 1966 for a way to go beyond the three-minute pop single. Through a friend he got to know the Indian spiritual teacher Meher Baba and tried to turn his ideas into music. Thus arose a story about Tommy Walker, a boy who seems deaf, dumb and blind and later becomes a spiritual leader. Recording began in September 1968 and lasted six months, because the material still had to be arranged and re-recorded in the studio.

The Who released Tommy as a double album and as one of the first rock operas on 19 May 1969. It won praise from critics and was regarded as the band's breakthrough. A long tour, including Woodstock and the Isle of Wight Festival, gave the group new strength. The story was later adapted into a ballet, a film in 1975 and a Broadway musical in 1992.
werk/the-who-tommy.listen: Listen to Pinball Wizard and notice how the story becomes light-hearted and hard-hitting at once here: Tommy turns out to be a master at pinball.

werk/the-who-who-are-you.text:
Three years lay between The Who by Numbers and this album. The band was drifting apart: the members worked on solo projects and Keith Moon and Pete Townshend sank deeper into drink and drugs. The sessions at Ramport Studios, under Glyn Johns and Jon Astley, went listlessly. Moon's drumming had deteriorated badly. On Music Must Change the drums were removed and replaced by footsteps and a few cymbal crashes. In addition, a throat operation for Roger Daltrey and the move to RAK Studios held up the recording.

Townshend wrote complicated arrangements with layers of synthesizer and strings and let songs return from his never-realised Lifehouse project. He also felt uncertain about the band's place after punk. Reviews were mixed, sales strong. Moon died three weeks after its release. On the cover he sits on a chair bearing the words Not to Be Taken Away.
werk/the-who-who-are-you.listen: Listen to Music Must Change and notice that Moon's drums are missing. Hear what sounds in their place.

werk/the-who-who-s-next.text:
After Tommy, Pete Townshend wanted something new: Lifehouse, a multimedia rock opera about a future in which music is forbidden. The project proved too complicated and led to a row with manager Kit Lambert, and was abandoned. The Who rescued the songs without the story around them. Eight of the nine songs come from Lifehouse, only My Wife is by John Entwistle. Engineer Glyn Johns helped with the recording, which took place largely at Olympic Studios.

Synthesizers play a striking role, especially in Baba O'Riley and Won't Get Fooled Again, which were both released as singles. The cover alludes to the monolith from the film 2001: A Space Odyssey: the band stands by a concrete pillar on a slag heap. The album was an immediate success with critics and public and is regarded by many as the group's best.
werk/the-who-who-s-next.listen: In Baba O'Riley, listen to the synthesizer, which is prominent in this song, and to how the band plays over it.

werk/thelonious-monk-brilliant-corners.text:
Brilliant Corners was Thelonious Monk's third album for Riverside and the first there of his own compositions. It came about in three sessions in October and December 1956 with two different quintets, including Sonny Rollins, Ernie Henry, Oscar Pettiford and Max Roach. The title piece proved so complicated that the band needed twenty-five takes without managing a complete version. Producer Orrin Keepnews edited the final recording together from several takes. On Pannonica the pianist plays celesta.

The structure of the title piece differs from both the usual song form and the blues: an A section of eight bars, a B section of seven and an altered A section of seven, with a double tempo in every second chorus. DownBeat called it the most acclaimed jazz record of 1957. The album has been added to the Library of Congress's National Recording Registry and was later seen as the pianist's return as a composer of the first rank.
werk/thelonious-monk-brilliant-corners.listen: In Pannonica, listen to the sound of the celesta that Monk plays himself and that makes this piece sound different from the rest of the album.

werk/thelonious-monk-piano-solo.text:
Piano Solo is a 1954 album by pianist and composer Thelonious Monk. He recorded it on 4 June 1954 in Paris, originally for a radio broadcast. The French firm Disques Vogue released it as a ten-inch record. Several titles were wrongly printed on the cover and his first name got an extra o. Over the years the music appeared under several titles, including on GNP Crescendo. Some editions contained Hackensack as an extra track.

The record consists mainly of his own compositions, such as 'Round About Midnight, Evidence, Well You Needn't, Eronel and Off Minor. Smoke Gets in Your Eyes by Jerome Kern is the only exception. In 2017 Sony released an expanded edition, in order of recording and with an announcement by André Francis and unreleased live tracks from the Salle Pleyel.
werk/thelonious-monk-piano-solo.listen: In 'Round About Midnight, listen to one of the pianist's own compositions, played entirely alone, without bass and drums.

werk/thelonious-monk-thelonious-himself.text:
Thelonious Himself was released in 1957 on Riverside Records, Thelonious Monk's fourth album for that label. He plays solo piano, except on the last track, Monk's Mood, on which John Coltrane on tenor saxophone and Wilbur Ware on bass join in. It was his second solo piano album in the studio and the first that an American label made and released in the United States. His first long solo recording, Piano Solo, had been made in Paris in June 1954. He recorded this album at Reeves Sound Studios, where he also sits at the mixing desk on the cover.

Robert Christgau called it probably his best solo album and Down Beat gave it five stars. Scott Yanow found it less important, but admired his hesitant stride and his considered, unpredictable excursions.
werk/thelonious-monk-thelonious-himself.listen: In Monk's Mood, listen to how Coltrane and Ware accompany the piano, on the only track that is not solo.

werk/thomas-anders-different.text:
Different is the first solo album by the German singer Thomas Anders, who became known in the mid-1980s as lead singer of Modern Talking. It was released in August 1989 on Teldec Records. The album was recorded in London at Alan Parsons's studio, with Gus Dudgeon (Elton John) and Alan Tarney (a-ha) as producers. Fool If You Think It's Over, a cover of Chris Rea, is on it.

The lead single Love of My Own reached number 24 in Germany. The album and the singles One Thing and Soldier did not enter the charts. In 1991 the record was reissued on CD, on East West Records. The album's working title had originally been Fool If You Think It's Over.
werk/thomas-anders-different.listen: Listen to Fool If You Think It's Over and notice what the singer makes of this song by Chris Rea.

werk/thomas-anders-down-on-sunset.text:
Down on Sunset was released in 1992 and is the third studio album by Thomas Anders. Ralf Stemmann and Christian De Walden produced it. It was recorded at the Flamingo Café Recording Studio in Los Angeles and mixed in Santa Monica. He co-wrote several songs under the name Chris Copperfield.

The album also contains a cover of Laughter in the Rain, the well-known song by Neil Sedaka. The singles released were How Deep Is Your Love and Standing Alone, the latter a duet with Glenn Medeiros. In Los Angeles, guitarist Tim Pierce and keyboard player Patrick Moraz, among others, took part, with a horn section and a string section added. In Japan the album was reissued the same year. In 1998 it came out again, this time under the title How Deep Is Your Love.
werk/thomas-anders-down-on-sunset.listen: Listen to Standing Alone and notice how the voices of Thomas Anders and Glenn Medeiros alternate and complement each other in this duet.

werk/thomas-anders-when-will-i-see-you-a.text:
When Will I See You Again is the fourth studio album by the German singer, songwriter and producer Thomas Anders. It was released in 1993 and, like its predecessor, was produced by Ralf Stemmann and Christian De Walden. It was recorded at the Flamingo Café Recording Studio in Studio City, California.

The title track is a new version of the classic by The Three Degrees, who sing along themselves in a duet. I'll Love You Forever and The Love in Me were also released as singles. Marathon of Life was written by Stemmann for the Swedish film Stockholm Marathon, in which he played a small role. The album also features guitarist Tim Pierce, saxophonist Doug Norwine and a string section from Los Angeles. It closes with an unplugged version of the title track.
werk/thomas-anders-when-will-i-see-you-a.listen: Listen to the duet When Will I See You Again and notice how The Three Degrees sing the familiar melody together with Anders.

werk/thomas-anders-whispers.text:
Whispers is the second studio album by Thomas Anders, released in 1991. Paul Muggleton and Mike Paxman, who also worked for Nick Kamen, produced the album, and Stephen W Tayler mixed it. Some of the songs come from writers for Roxette (Per Gessle) and Jennifer Rush (Candy DeRouge). The opener The Sweet Hello, the Sad Goodbye is by Per Gessle.

The album contains a remake of the classic Can't Give You Anything (But My Love) by The Stylistics, which was also released as a separate video clip. Judie Tzuke and Don Snow, formerly of Squeeze, sing backing vocals. East West Records released the record in, among other countries, Germany and France.
werk/thomas-anders-whispers.listen: Listen to Can't Give You Anything (But My Love) and compare the remake with the original by The Stylistics.

werk/throbbing-gristle-20-jazz-funk-grea.text:
This third album, released in December 1979 on Industrial Records, was Throbbing Gristle's first full studio record. Earlier albums also contained live recordings. The group recorded it at their own Death Factory in Hackney, on a 16-track recorder that had been borrowed from Paul McCartney via Peter Christopherson. Many of the electronic instruments and effects came from Roland and Boss, and some had been designed or modified by the band themselves.

The title and the cover are a joke. The photograph was taken at Beachy Head, a notorious suicide spot. The design imitated the supermarket bargain bin, to mislead buyers. The music hides the band's noise inside electronic rhythms, with influences of exotica and disco. According to one critic, Hot on Heels of Love is convincing disco in the style of Moroder. Fact called it the best record of the 1970s, Pitchfork the best industrial record ever.
werk/throbbing-gristle-20-jazz-funk-grea.listen: Listen to Hot on Heels of Love and notice the bubbling synthesizers and the cracking snare. How does this fit with the disco of Moroder?

werk/thundercat-drunk.text:
Thundercat released Drunk on 24 February 2017 on Brainfeeder, almost four years after his previous studio album Apocalypse. The album contains dozens of short tracks and a string of guests, including Kenny Loggins, Michael McDonald, Kendrick Lamar, Wiz Khalifa, Mac Miller, Pharrell and Kamasi Washington. The style is broad: funk, hip hop, jazz, pop, psychedelia, R&B, soft rock and soul. One reviewer heard the record switch suddenly between Cool Jazz, prog fusion and smooth soul.

The lyrics are often about drink, drugs and partying, but also about loss and death. In Bus in These Streets the subject is too much smartphone use. A Fan's Mail (Tron Song Suite II) is partly named after his cat Tron, and the chorus consists of meowing sounds. Show You the Way, with McDonald and Loggins, was described as yacht rock. Them Changes uses a beat from a song by the Isley Brothers. The reviews were positive.
werk/thundercat-drunk.listen: Listen to Show You the Way and notice how Michael McDonald and Kenny Loggins give the song a soft, almost yacht rock feel.

werk/tigran-hamasyan-luys-i-luso.text:
Luys i Luso means Light from the Light in Armenian and is the seventh album by pianist Tigran Hamasyan. He made it to commemorate one hundred years of the Armenian genocide. For three years he collected and arranged Armenian sacred music, from sharakans of the fifth century to hymns from the early twentieth century. In October 2014 he recorded the album with the Yerevan State Chamber Choir, conducted by Harutyun Topikyan, and with Manfred Eicher of ECM as producer.

The music is written for piano, prepared piano and voices. Hamasyan lays improvised piano and vocal percussion over the arranged choral singing. Surb Astvats tells the story of Christ, and Hayrapetakan Maghterg comes from Komitas. The work was subsequently performed in a hundred churches around the world. Hamasyan himself calls it a musical world in which tradition, contemporary composition and improvisation come together.
werk/tigran-hamasyan-luys-i-luso.listen: Listen to Nor Tsaghik and notice how the choir voices and the piano complement each other in a long and complex piece.
